subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw add a model-facing browser network inspection/interception action, and should the first supported API be passive-only or include active request mutation?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing authenticated browser traffic to the model changes the browser security boundary and needs maintainer-owned policy for redaction, permissions, profile support, and whether active interception is acceptable.

options.title: Passive inspected output first
options.body: Expose bounded request listing and response-body matching through the browser plugin with redaction/profile limits, and defer active interception or mutation until the policy is proven.

options.title: Full CDP interception
options.body: Add active request interception and mutation now, accepting the larger security and compatibility review burden before implementation.

options.title: Keep control API only
options.body: Leave request inspection in the CLI/control API for trusted operators and do not expose it to model-facing browser tool calls yet.

recommendation.title: Passive inspected output first
recommendation.body: Expose bounded request listing and response-body matching through the browser plugin with redaction/profile limits, and defer active interception or mutation until the policy is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest feature-history owner for the browser plugin/tool schema and route surfaces that would carry this decision.
